title: Draupadi Appeals to Krishna for Vengeance
one_line_summary: Draupadi, clutching her dishevelled hair, reminds Krishna of her humiliation in the assembly and begs him to avenge her on the Kauravas.
source_excerpt: Lotus-eyed one that art anxious for peace with the enemy, thou shouldst, in all thy acts, call to thy mind these tresses of mine seized by Dussasana's rude hands! ... What peace can this heart of mine know unless I behold Dussasana's dark arm severed from his trunk and pulverised to atoms?

title: Krishna Vows the Kuru Women Will Weep
one_line_summary: Krishna comforts the weeping Draupadi and swears that the women of the Kuru race will soon weep as she does, with their kinsmen slain.
source_excerpt: The mighty-armed Kesava then spoke, comforting her in these words, 'Soon wilt thou, O Krishna, behold the ladies of Bharata's race weep as thou dost... The mountains of Himavat might shift their site, the Earth herself might split into a hundred fragments... still my words can never be futile. Stop thy tears, I swear to thee, O Krishna, soon wilt thou see thy husbands, with their enemies slain, and with prosperity crowning them.'

title: Krishna Accepts the Peace Mission
one_line_summary: Asked by Arjuna to go as envoy, Krishna agrees to go to Dhritarashtra to seek peace for the good of both the Pandavas and the Kurus.
source_excerpt: The holy one said, 'Yes, I will go to king Dhritarashtra, desirous of accomplishing what is consistent with righteousness, what may be beneficial to us, and what also is for the good of the Kurus.'

title: Krishna Prepares His Chariot and Sets Out for Hastinapura
one_line_summary: After his morning rites, Krishna has his car armed with his conch, discus and mace; Garuda alights on its flagstaff, and he mounts and sets out with Satyaki.
source_excerpt: And they yoked unto it those excellent steeds named Saivya and Sugriva and Meghapushpa and Valahaka... Garuda, the lord of the feathery creation, came and perched on the flag-staff of that car producing a terrible rattle. And Saurin then mounted on that car, high as the summit of the Meru... And taking Satyaki also upon it, that best of male beings set out.

title: Yudhishthira Entrusts Krishna with Messages for Kunti and the Elders
one_line_summary: Yudhishthira, following Krishna some distance, asks him to salute and comfort his grieving mother Kunti and to greet Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Vidura and all the elders.
source_excerpt: Yudhishthira said, 'That lady who hath brought us from our infancy... should be asked about her welfare--Salute and embrace, and, oh, comfort her over and over, overwhelmed with grief as she is on account of her sons... Salute her for me, the Kuru king Dhritarashtra also... and Bhishma, and Drona, and Kripa... and also Vidura endued with great wisdom.'

title: Arjuna's Parting Warning and Bhima's Roar
one_line_summary: Arjuna warns that if Duryodhana acts improperly he will annihilate the Kshatriyas, and Bhima, hearing this, sets forth a terrible shout that makes all bowmen tremble.
source_excerpt: Then Arjuna, proceeding a few steps, further said... 'If, however, Dhritarashtra's son, who always adopts improper means, acts otherwise, then I shall surely, O Janardana, annihilate the Kshatriya race.' ... he set forth a terrible shout. And hearing that shout of his, all the bowmen trembled in fear and steeds and elephants were seen to pass urine and excreta.

title: Krishna Meets the Celestial Rishis Led by Parashurama
one_line_summary: On the road Krishna alights to worship a band of celestial Rishis; Jamadagni's son Parashurama embraces him and says they come to witness the conclave and hear his words.
source_excerpt: on his way Kesava of mighty arms met with some Rishis blazing with Brahmic lustre... Jamadagni's son... approached Govinda the slayer of Madhu, embraced him, and said, '...We are desirous of beholding all the Kshatriyas of the earth assembled from every side... We are also anxious... to listen to those words fraught with virtue and profit, which will be spoken by thee... unto the Kurus in the presence of all the kings.'

title: Krishna's Auspicious Journey to Hastinapura
one_line_summary: As Krishna journeys to Hastinapura, dread omens fall on the Kuru capital while wherever he passes the road becomes auspicious with showers of flowers; he passes the night at Vrikasthala.
source_excerpt: Though there were no clouds in the sky, yet the roll of thunder accompanied by flashes of lightning was heard... A south-westerly wind, with the harsh rattle of the thunder, uprooting trees by the thousands, crushed the city of Hastinapura. In those places, however, O Bharata, through which he of Vrishni's race passed, delicious breezes blew and everything became auspicious. Showers of lotuses and fragrant flowers fell there.

title: Duryodhana's Lavish Pavilions That Krishna Ignores
one_line_summary: Duryodhana builds gem-studded pavilions to receive Krishna, but Krishna arrives at the Kuru capital without casting a single glance at them.
source_excerpt: And the king of the Kurus took especial care to erect, for the reception of Krishna, a highly beautiful pavilion at Vrikasthala, full of precious gems... Kesava, however, of Dasarha's race, arrived at the capital of the Kurus, without casting a single glance at all those pavilions and all those gems of diverse kinds.

title: Vidura Exposes the Plan to Bribe Krishna
one_line_summary: When Dhritarashtra plans lavish gifts to win Krishna over, Vidura declares the gifts betray deception and that Krishna can never be separated from Arjuna.
source_excerpt: Vidura said, '...Know, however, that Kesava deserves all this and much more, aye, the whole earth itself... By the external acts, O king, I know thy secret purpose. The five Pandavas, O king, desire only five villages. Thou, however, dost not wish to give them even that... thou seekest to separate Kesava from the Pandavas. I tell thee, however, that thou art unable, by wealth, or attention, or worship, to separate Krishna from Dhananjaya.'

title: Duryodhana Resolves to Imprison Krishna; Bhishma Departs in Anger
one_line_summary: Duryodhana announces his plan to imprison Krishna; Dhritarashtra is pained and Bhishma, denouncing the wicked scheme, rises in rage and leaves.
source_excerpt: Duryodhana said, '...I will imprison Janardana who is the refuge of the Pandavas. He will come here tomorrow morning; and when he is confined, the Vrishnis and the Pandavas, aye, the whole earth, will submit to me.' ... Bhishma said, 'This wicked son of thine, O Dhritarashtra, hath his hour come... Having said this, that aged chief of the Bharata race, Bhishma of unbaffled prowess, inflamed with rage rose and left that place.

title: Krishna Enters Hastinapura and Meets Dhritarashtra
one_line_summary: Welcomed by Bhishma, Drona and the Dhartarashtras, Krishna enters Hastinapura, where the blind king Dhritarashtra and all the elders rise to honour him.
source_excerpt: And meeting on the way Bhishma of spotless deed, and Drona, and Dhritarashtra's sons, he entered the city, surrounded by them all... And that lotus-eyed grinder of foes then entered Dhritarashtra's ash-coloured palace... the blind monarch of great fame stood up along with Drona and Bhishma, Kripa and Somadatta, and king Vahlika also.

title: Krishna Comforts the Grieving Kunti
one_line_summary: Krishna visits his aunt Kunti, who pours out her sorrows for her exiled sons; he consoles her and assures her she will soon see the Pandavas victorious.
source_excerpt: Vasudeva said, 'What woman is there, O aunt, in the world who is like thee?... Endued with every virtue, and endued with great wisdom, it behoveth thee to bear with patience, both happiness and misery... The Pandavas with Krishna saluteth thee through me... Thou wilt soon behold them become the lords of the whole world, with their foe slain, and themselves invested with prosperity.'

title: Krishna Refuses Duryodhana's Hospitality
one_line_summary: Duryodhana invites Krishna to eat at his house, but Krishna refuses, saying envoys eat only after their mission succeeds and that he will accept food from Vidura alone.
source_excerpt: The high-souled Govinda... replied... saying, 'Envoys, O king, eat and accept worship only after the success of their missions...' ... 'Defiled by wickedness, all this food, therefore, deserveth not to be eaten by me. The food supplied by Vidura alone, should, I think, be eaten by me.'

title: Vidura Warns Krishna of Duryodhana's Wickedness
one_line_summary: That night Vidura tells Krishna his coming was ill-judged, describing Duryodhana's vices and his belief that he can never be persuaded to make peace.
source_excerpt: Vidura said unto him during the night, 'O Kesava, this advent of thine hath not been a well judged one, for, O Janardana, Dhritarashtra's son transgresseth the rules of both profit and religion, is wicked and wrathful... He will, therefore, never make peace.'

title: Krishna's Resolve: The Merit of Striving for Peace
one_line_summary: Krishna answers Vidura that he came knowing Duryodhana's wickedness, for great is the merit of one who strives to save the earth from destruction even if he fails.
source_excerpt: The holy one said, '...Well knowing the wickedness of Dhritarashtra's son and the hostility of the Kshatriyas that have sided with him, I have still, O Vidura, come to the Kurus. Great will be the merit earned by him who will liberate from the meshes of death the whole earth, with her elephants, cars and steeds, overwhelmed with a dreadful calamity.'

title: Krishna Enters the Kuru Assembly
one_line_summary: Krishna rides in procession to the Kuru court, enters arm-in-arm with Vidura and Satyaki, and after the Rishis are seated takes his seat in the assembly.
source_excerpt: And having reached the gate of the court, Sauri, that bull among the Satwatas, alighting from his car... entered the court which looked like a mass of newly-risen clouds... And that illustrious hero entered the court, arm-in-arm with Vidura and Satyaki on either side, and overshadowing with his own the splendour of all the Kurus.

title: Krishna's Plea for Peace Before the Assembly
one_line_summary: Before the assembled kings, Krishna urges Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons and restore the Pandavas' share of the kingdom, to save the world from slaughter.
source_excerpt: In order that, O Bharata, peace may be established between the Kurus and the Pandavas without a slaughter of the heroes, I have come hither... Save, O king, the world. Let not the population of the earth be exterminated... Giving unto the Pandavas their just share of the paternal kingdom, enjoy thou then, with thy sons, O chastiser of foes, happiness and luxury.

title: Parashurama Reveals Krishna and Arjuna as Nara and Narayana
one_line_summary: Parashurama, in the assembly, tells the tale of Dambhodbhava and declares that Nara and Narayana of old are now Arjuna and Krishna, urging Duryodhana to make peace.
source_excerpt: Rama continued, '...They that were Nara and Narayana in days of yore are now Arjuna and Kesava. Know then, O great king, who those brave and foremost of persons are. If thou believest in this and dost not mistrust me adopt thou a virtuous resolution and make peace with the sons of Pandu.'

title: Krishna's Appeal to Duryodhana
one_line_summary: At Dhritarashtra's request, Krishna approaches Duryodhana directly and urges him, with reasoned counsel, to make peace with the Pandavas for the good of his own race.
source_excerpt: The mighty-armed Govinda... said unto him these sweet words, 'O Duryodhana, O best of the Kurus, listen to these words of mine, uttered especially for thy good... Then, O tiger among men, make peace, O bull among the Bharatas, with the sons of Pandu who are all endued with great wisdom and great bravery...'

title: Duryodhana's Refusal: Not a Needle-Point of Land
one_line_summary: Duryodhana rejects Krishna's counsel, claiming he has done no wrong, and vows that not even land covered by the point of a needle will be given to the Pandavas while he lives.
source_excerpt: Duryodhana replied... 'As long, O Janardana, as king Dhritarashtra liveth, both ourselves and they... should live in dependence on him... even that much of our land which may be covered by the point of a sharp needle shall not, O Madhava, be given by us unto the Pandavas.'

title: Krishna's Rebuke of Duryodhana's Crimes
one_line_summary: With eyes red in anger, Krishna recounts Duryodhana's crimes — the dice plot, Draupadi's humiliation, the attempts to burn and poison the Pandavas — and foretells his downfall.
source_excerpt: he, of Dasarha's race, addressing Duryodhana... said these words, 'Wishest thou for a bed of heroes? Verily, thou shalt have it, with thy counsellors... Who else is there, capable of insulting a brother's wife in the way thou didst or of dragging her into the assembly and addressing her in language thou hadst used towards Draupadi?'

title: Krishna Urges the Elders to Bind Duryodhana
one_line_summary: After Duryodhana storms out, Krishna tells the elders that they are guilty for not seizing the wicked king, citing how he himself slew Kansa to save his kinsmen.
source_excerpt: Kesava... said, 'Even this is great transgression, of which all the elders of the Kuru race are becoming guilty, for they do not forcibly seize and bind this wicked king... Kansa, the son of Ugrasena, abandoned by his relatives, was slain by me in a great encounter, from desire of benefiting my kinsmen... binding Duryodhana fast, make peace with the Pandavas.'

title: The Plot to Seize Krishna; Satyaki's Alarm
one_line_summary: Duryodhana, Karna, Sakuni and Dussasana resolve to seize Krishna by force; Satyaki, reading the signs, alerts Krishna and arrays the troops.
source_excerpt: this was the resolution which Duryodhana and Karna and Suvala's son Sakuni, with Dussasana as their fourth, arrived at, 'This Janardana, quick in action, seeketh... to seize us first. We, however, shall forcibly seize this tiger among men, Hrishikesa, first, like Indra forcibly seizing Virochana's son.' ... Satyaki, capable of reading the heart by signs, soon came to know of it.

title: Krishna Defies the Conspirators
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Dhritarashtra that if they wish to seize him by violence they may try, for he could make over all of them to the Pandavas, but he will not commit a censurable deed.
source_excerpt: Kesava, casting his eyes on Dhritarashtra, said... 'O king, if these (men) desire to chastise me by using violence, permit them to chastise me... this very day, O Bharata, seizing these with all that follow them, I can make them over to the sons of Pritha... I will not, however, O Bharata, commit in thy presence, O great monarch, any such censurable deed.'

title: Krishna Reveals His Universal Form
one_line_summary: Laughing at Duryodhana's boast to seize him, Krishna bursts into his universal form — gods issuing from his body, the whole court dazzled, all but a few closing their eyes in terror.
source_excerpt: And as the high-souled Sauri laughed, from his body, that resembled a blazing fire, issued myriads of gods, each of lightning effulgence, and not bigger than the thumb. And on his forehead appeared Brahman, and on his breast Rudra... And beholding that awful form of the high-souled Kesava, all the kings closed their eyes with affrighted hearts, except Drona, and Bhishma, and Vidura... and Sanjaya... for the divine Janardana gave unto them this divine sight on the occasion.

title: Krishna Departs as Dhritarashtra Pleads Powerlessness
one_line_summary: With the assembly witnessed, Krishna takes leave of the elders, declares he will return to Yudhishthira, and mounts his car to depart as Dhritarashtra protests his powerlessness.
source_excerpt: The mighty-armed Janardana then addressed Dhritarashtra, Drona, grandsire Bhishma, Kshattri, Vahlika, and Kripa and said, 'Ye have yourselves witnessed all that hath happened in the assembly of the Kurus... With the permission of you all, I shall now go back to Yudhishthira.' Saluting them, that bull amongst men, Sauri then mounted his car and set out.

title: Krishna Relays Kunti's Message: The Duty of a Kshatriya
one_line_summary: Krishna reports the failed embassy to Kunti and carries back her charge to Yudhishthira to recover his kingdom by the prowess of his arms as a Kshatriya should.
source_excerpt: Kunti said, 'O Kesava, say unto king Yudhishthira of virtuous soul these words, "Thy virtue, O son, is decreasing greatly. Do not act vainly... Thou art a Kshatriya and therefore, the protector of all in distress. Thou art to live by the prowess of thy arms. O thou of mighty arms, recover thy paternal share of the kingdom which thou hast lost..."'

title: Kunti's Exhortation: The Story of Vidula and Sanjaya
one_line_summary: Kunti instructs Krishna to carry the ancient tale of Vidula, who shamed her defeated son Sanjaya back into battle, as an exhortation to war for Yudhishthira.
source_excerpt: Kunti said, 'In this connection, O chastiser of foes, is cited an old story of the conversation between Vidula and her son... There was a high-born dame of great foresight, named Vidula... the princess Vidula, one day, rebuked her own son, who, after his defeat by the king of the Sindhus, lay prostrate with heart depressed by despair.'
notes: The Vidula-Sanjaya discourse runs through sections 133-136; condensed here as a single beat since Krishna is only the bearer of the message.

title: Kunti's Final Messages and Krishna's Leave-Taking
one_line_summary: Kunti gives Krishna parting words for Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi and the twins, recalling the celestial voice that promised Arjuna victory, and Krishna takes his leave of her.
source_excerpt: Kunti said, 'Say unto Arjuna, these words... "when thou wert brought forth in the lying-in room... a celestial and delightful voice was heard in the sky, saying... 'This one will vanquish in battle all the assembled Kurus...'"... Go thou on thy auspicious way, and protect my sons!'

title: Krishna Takes Karna Upon His Chariot and Returns to Upaplavya
one_line_summary: Krishna dismisses the Kuru chiefs, takes Karna upon his chariot, deliberates with him at length, then dismisses him and returns swiftly to Upaplavya.
source_excerpt: And he then dismissed those chiefs among the Kurus with Bhishma at their head, and taking Karna upon his chariot, left (the Kuru city), accompanied by Satyaki... Having issued out of the (Kuru) city, that foremost of persons proceeded, deliberating with Karna for a long time... And quickly traversing a long way like fleet hawks, they reached Upaplavya very soon.
notes: The dialogue between Krishna and Karna during this ride is narrated retrospectively by Sanjaya in sections 140-141.

title: Krishna Reveals Karna's Birth and Offers Him the Kingdom
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Karna he is Kunti's firstborn son and therefore a Pandava, and offers to have him installed as king of the whole earth with the Pandavas as his followers.
source_excerpt: Vasudeva said, 'O son of Radha, thou hast worshipped many Brahmanas fully conversant with the Vedas... It is said by those conversant with the scriptures that the two kinds of sons called Kanina and Sahoda... have him for their father who weddeth the maid. Thou, O Karna, hast been born in this way. Thou art, therefore, morally the son of Pandu. Come, be a king, according to the injunction of the scriptures... let the Pandavas know thee as a son of Kunti born before Yudhishthira... install thee as the lord of the whole earth.'

title: Karna Refuses, Pledging Loyalty to Duryodhana
one_line_summary: Acknowledging he is Kunti's son by Surya, Karna refuses the kingdom, declaring that Adhiratha and Radha who raised him are his parents and that he will not betray Duryodhana.
source_excerpt: Karna said, '...Morally, I am the son of Pandu... Kunti, however, abandoned me without thinking of my welfare. The Suta, Adhiratha, as soon as he beheld me, took me to his home... I cannot venture, O Janardana, to behave falsely towards the intelligent son of Dhritarashtra... If king Yudhishthira... cometh to know me as the firstborn son of Kunti, he will never accept the kingdom.'

title: Karna's Prophecy of the Coming War as a Sacrifice
one_line_summary: Karna foretells the war as a great sacrifice of arms with Krishna as its witness, describing how each hero will play a priestly part, and asks Krishna to keep their talk secret.
source_excerpt: a great sacrifice of arms is about to be celebrated by Dhritarashtra's son. Thou, O Janardana, wilt be the Upadrashtri of that sacrifice... The ape-bannered Vibhatsu accoutred in mail will be the Hotri... When mighty Bhimasena will slay Duryodhana, then, O Madhava, will this sacrifice of Dhritarashtra's son be concluded... bring Kunti's son (Arjuna) before me for battle, keeping for ever this our discourse a secret.
